key_insight: Combining white matter fiber orientation distributions with rotation-equivariant deep learning improved brain age prediction while revealing age-dependent anatomical sensitivity.
engineering_relevance: For biomedical imaging systems, respecting the rotational geometry of orientation-dependent features can improve predictive performance over scalar inputs and conventional CNNs.
method: Represent diffusion MRI white matter fiber orientations using spherical harmonic coefficients.
Process coefficients with an SE(3)-equivariant CNN that preserves their transformation properties under rotation.
Mask individual white matter tracts to assess age-dependent model sensitivity.
evidence_signal: In 692 HCP Aging participants aged 36–90, averaging predictions from five cross-validation models achieved 3.54-year MAE and Pearson r = 0.958, outperforming evaluated DTI-based models and conventional CNNs.
watch_item: External-cohort validation is not reported in the abstract, and accuracy declined above the best-performing spherical harmonic order, Lmax = 2.
paper_title: Interpretable Brain Age Prediction Using White Matter Fiber Orientation Distributions with Rotation-Equivariant Deep Learning
